summary: Branch-office egress TSO + VPCE path causes intermittent MTLS/OCSP timeouts and partial shard validation
description:
Issue summary: Customer's private deployment behind a branch-office NAT appliance is experiencing intermittent timeouts during control-plane mTLS handshake and OCSP stapling verification, and occasional model shard validation failures (range GET SHA mismatch).
Impact: Customers report increased 5xx/timeout errors for model pulls and transient inference failures for a small percentage (~0.7%) of requests during nightly batch loads. Production latency impact for affected requests: 2-10s additional retries; some requests fail end-to-end.
Environment: Private deployment using VPCE to access Redwood control plane and S3 presigned artifact storage. Branch office egress appliance with TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) enabled and on-path WAN optimizer.
Steps to reproduce:
  1) From branch office host behind NAT appliance, trigger model prefetch for rwd-open-13b-quant (range GETs).
  2) Observe OCSP stapling and mTLS handshake with control-plane endpoints via VPCE.
  3) During high-concurrency batch fetch (parallel shard downloads x32), ~1% of shards fail with truncated range content or TLS handshake timeouts.
Logs / Observed symptoms:
  - client: "TLS handshake timeout after 7s (tcp_retransmits=3)"
  - control-plane: "mTLS: OCSP response verify failed: short_read"
  - artifact service: "range GET returned content-length 0 for shard 00012 (expected 3.2MB)"
  - branch NAT logs: "TSO segmented packet exceed MSS, dropping segment"
 Additional context: Failures correlate with times when the branch egress appliance offloads segmentation and rewrites TCP options (SACK/ECN) and when VPCE path traverses a WAN optimizer performing MSS clamping.
Customer impact window: first observed 2026-03-12 23:40 UTC, intermittent since then, peaked during nightly batch on 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC.
investigation_notes: 03/14 03:05 UTC - Initial triage by Support: verified customer network path uses VPCE with on-path egress NAT appliance and WAN optimizer. Reproduced partial shard failures when batch-concurrency >= 16.

03/14 03:22 UTC - Gathered packet captures from customer (pcap provided): observed IP fragmentation/overlapping TCP sequence ranges and MSS mismatch between host and egress appliance. Egress appliance shows TSO on but reports MSS clamp to 1200 bytes on the uplink.

03/14 03:40 UTC - Correlation found with OCSP stapling failures: control-plane logs show TLS record layer truncation after stall; OCSP responder returns truncated payload when upstream connection resets. Hypothesis: TSO + MSS clamping causes middlebox to send improperly segmented TLS records leading to TLS/Ocsp parser read errors.

03/14 04:10 UTC - Eng (network infra) ran a controlled test: disable TSO on branch host VM and rerun batch prefetch. Result: no shard truncation observed across 10k range GETs; mTLS handshakes succeeded consistently.
    Hypothesis strengthened: TSO combined with asymmetric MSS rewrite is causing out-of-spec segment sizes resulting in TLS record reassembly failures on the VPCE-terminating proxy or OCSP path.

03/14 04:45 UTC - Checked related infra: VPCE endpoint service (internal NLB) is not modifying TCP options; observed failure happens before VPCE ingress (on egress path). Logged correlation with our existing ticket SUP-712987 (ocsp staple break during proxy injection).
03/14 05:20 UTC - Customer provided firewall config: 'accelerate_tcp true', 'tso on', and explicit MSS clamping rule to 1200. Suggested temporary disable of TSO and to remove MSS clamp for test.
03/14 06:00 UTC - Customer applied temporary change: disabled TSO on hosts and bypassed WAN optimizer for VPCE IP range. Monitoring: error rate for shard downloads dropped to baseline (<0.05%).
comments: 2026-03-14 03:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Initial intake. Collected pcap, shard hashes, and customer topology diagram. Escalated to Network Infra.

2026-03-14 03:35 - Network Infra (Marco Diaz): Running packet-level triage. Seeing MSS/TCP option mismatch and mid-connection segment reassembly errors at upstream proxy. Adding Eng for deeper analysis.

2026-03-14 04:20 - Customer (BrightPath Health, NetOps - Jordan Lee): Applied test to disable TSO on a single host and re-ran fetch job. Attaching logs - observed immediate improvement. Asking if this aligns with Redwood recommendations.

2026-03-14 05:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Confirmed improvement. Recommended temporary mitigation: disable TSO on hosts that access VPCE or add explicit bypass rule for VPCE destination CIDRs on WAN optimizer. Documented steps and asked NetOps to schedule permanent fix.

2026-03-14 06:30 - Network Infra (Marco Diaz): Will follow up with a runbook addition: 'When using VPCE with WAN optimizer, ensure TSO/GRO disabled or configure consistent MSS across path'. Filing infra task to monitor similar customer telemetry.

2026-03-14 07:10 - Customer (Jordan Lee): Scheduling maintenance window to remove MSS clamp and to upgrade WAN optimizer firmware. Marking current change as successful; will report if recurs after full rollout.
resolution:
Mitigation: Customer disabled TSO on branch hosts and added VPCE CIDR bypass on their WAN optimizer which eliminated the shard truncation and mTLS/OCSP errors in observed tests. Root cause: interaction between TCP Segmentation Offload (host-side) and an on-path MSS clamping WAN optimizer that produced out-of-spec TCP segments leading to TLS record truncation and OCSP read failures.
Permanent fix/action items:
  - Recommend customer: disable TSO/GRO for hosts that fetch model artifacts via VPCE OR ensure WAN optimizer does not MSS-clamp below path MTU.
  - Redwood: add a KB article and console alert guidance for private deployments warning about TSO/GRO + MSS clamping interactions with VPCE endpoints.
  - Infra: add automated telemetry to detect increased TLS record fragmentation / short_read OCSP errors and surface to support dashboard.
Follow-up: Customer to confirm after WAN optimizer firmware upgrade and removal of MSS clamp. Support will keep ticket open until customer confirms 72-hour healthy window.
